mainEntity.name: How long does ridge expansion take to heal completely?

acceptedAnswer.text: Complete healing typically requires 4-6 months, during which the bone graft integrates with your natural bone. Initial soft tissue healing occurs within 2-3 weeks, but the bone remodelling process continues for several months. Your dentist will monitor healing progress through regular appointments and may use imaging to confirm adequate bone formation before proceeding with implant placement.

mainEntity.name: Is ridge expansion more painful than dental implant surgery?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most patients report similar comfort levels between ridge expansion and implant placement procedures. Both treatments are performed under local anaesthesia, and any post-operative discomfort typically responds well to prescribed pain relief. The healing period may involve some swelling and sensitivity, but following post-operative instructions helps minimise these effects significantly.

mainEntity.name: Can ridge expansion fail or not work properly?

acceptedAnswer.text: Whilst ridge expansion can achieve good outcomes in suitable cases, individual factors can influence results. Smoking, poor oral hygiene, certain medical conditions, or inadequate healing time may affect results. Following your dentist's instructions carefully, maintaining excellent oral hygiene, and attending all follow-up appointments help optimise healing and treatment success.

mainEntity.name: Will I need ridge expansion if I get implants immediately after extraction?

acceptedAnswer.text: Immediate implant placement may reduce the need for ridge expansion, but this depends on individual circumstances. If adequate bone width exists at the time of extraction, immediate implants can often be placed successfully. However, if the extraction socket is too wide or bone damage exists, additional bone grafting may still be necessary.

mainEntity.name: How much does ridge expansion cost compared to standard implant treatment?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ridge expansion involves additional procedures and materials beyond standard implant placement, which affects overall treatment costs. The specific techniques required, amount of bone grafting needed, and complexity of your case influence pricing. Your dentist will provide a detailed treatment plan including all necessary procedures and associated costs during your consultation.

mainEntity.name: Can multiple teeth areas be treated with ridge expansion simultaneously?

acceptedAnswer.text: Treating multiple areas during one procedure is often possible and can be more convenient for patients. However, the decision depends on factors including the extent of bone grafting required, your overall health, and healing capacity. Your dental surgeon will recommend the most appropriate approach based on your individual circumstances and treatment goals.
